metadata.title: Reviewer Judgment Framework
metadata.description: A shared reviewer judgment pack for competing interpretations, evidence sufficiency, confidence calibration, reviewer disagreement, narrative justification, and final reviewer decision making.

pack.title: Reviewer Judgment Framework
pack.purpose: Teach reviewers how experienced GCAM reviewers compare interpretations, judge evidence sufficiency, calibrate confidence, resolve disagreement, justify narrative outcomes, and make a final decision.
required_evidence: Literal evidence from the current chunk
Speaker and target cues when available
insufficient_evidence: Premature certainty before disagreement is resolved
reviewer_heuristics: List competing interpretations before choosing one.
Treat one clue as a hypothesis, not a conclusion.
Ask whether the evidence is sufficient or merely plausible.
Calibrate confidence to corroboration and contradiction.
Resolve disagreement before producing a final decision.
Use narrative justification when the story changes the meaning of a harmful-looking line.
Record the final decision only after the reviewer has exhausted the relevant context.
positive_examples: The reviewer compares two plausible readings before deciding.
The reviewer lowers confidence when a later sentence contradicts the first reading.
The reviewer keeps the case as review until the context becomes sufficient.
The reviewer explains why the story changes the final outcome.
The reviewer resolves disagreement instead of pretending it does not exist.
negative_examples: The reviewer accepts the first plausible reading.
The reviewer treats weak evidence as decisive.
The reviewer ignores disagreement between scenes.
The reviewer applies a final judgment before checking narrative justification.
common_false_positives: Collapsing review disagreement into one false answer
Using narrative justification as an excuse to skip evidence
Producing a final decision before evidence sufficiency is checked

glossary_relationships.note: Decide whether the evidence is enough.
Legitimate reviewer disagreement must be represented.
Story context may change the reviewer outcome.
The final reviewer decision is the output of judgment.

article_mapping.note: Reviewer judgment begins with comparing interpretations.
Reviewer judgment evaluates whether evidence is enough.
Reviewer judgment calibrates confidence and handles exceptions.

reporting_guidance: State the competing interpretations before the final answer.
Explain why the evidence is sufficient or insufficient.
Show how confidence changed when the context changed.
Name legitimate reviewer disagreement instead of hiding it.
If narrative justification changes the result, say so explicitly.
Finalize the report only after the judgment process is complete.
